rulings.challenge_claim: Convergent on one row. One challenge holds that the close taken at 5:11 carries no disclosed voice, addressee or discourse-frame marker, and that the ground used to set aside a cut after 5:6 would equally indict the chosen close. The other holds that the close cuts a byte-marked four-verse block after its first member with no weighing from either side, that both petition-onset digits misname what they count, and that the onset is called a doubled imperative where the verse carries three.
rulings.grounds: Same defect at the seam in both challenges; the digit and form-class items are distinct additions carried by only one of them. SEAM (upheld, tier-1). Re-derived from the pointed text of the whole poem: 5:11-5:14 each open with a bare plural human-group noun - נָשִׁים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.11, byte tier), שָׂרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.12, byte tier), בַּחוּרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.13, byte tier), זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.14, byte tier) - each followed by a third-plural verb, and none of the four carries a first-person-plural form (sweep: 0 first-plural-suffix or first-plural-verb tokens over those 4 verses; the single plural-ending token at 5:11 is a third-plural perfect). That is a tier-1 participant-run repetition straddling the unit's own close, disclosed nowhere. CORRECTION to the challenge's exclusivity: neither test is exclusive alone - the same verse-initial bare plural human-group noun stands at 5:3 and 5:8 (sweep: 6 verses in this poem carry that onset: 5:3, 5:8, 5:11, 5:12, 5:13, 5:14), and 5:18 also carries no first-plural form (sweep: 5 verses of 5:1-5:18 carry none: 5:11, 5:12, 5:13, 5:14, 5:18); it is the CONJUNCTION of the two tests that is exclusive, holding in exactly 4 verses, 5:11-5:14, the only consecutive run of any length in the poem (sweep: 4 verses of 22). The unit's own cited texture does not close at 5:11 either: the divine name stands at 5:1, 5:19 and 5:21 and nowhere between (sweep: 3 verses in this poem), so the absence of further direct address runs unbroken through 5:18 and cannot mark a close at 5:11. The ground offered against a cut after 5:6 - no voice or addressee shift - is equally true at the close actually taken, so the unit fails its own stated criterion. DIGITS (upheld). As a petition imperative the remember-form stands in 2 verses, not 3: the third site of the root is a negated third-person perfect, וְלֹא זָכַ֥ר (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier), with the divine title as its subject and no address. The look-imperative digit of 2 is a bare-token count; the same imperative stands behind a single vav at 1:11 and 2:20 - וְֽהַבִּ֔יטָה (oshb:Lam.1.11, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the desirable-things term, not at this run) and the byte-identical run at oshb:Lam.2.20 (byte tier) - so under this book's own single-letter prefix-tolerance test the form stands in 4 verses (1:11, 2:20, 3:63, 5:1). Both digits ship without naming their swept object, which is why one overstates and the other understates. FORM-CLASS (upheld). The onset is a three-imperative chain, not a doubled one: the third is וּרְאֵ֥ה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the look-imperative that the unit splices and discloses). NEW FINDING against the challenge's own supporting digit: the look-form census cited there as 7 sites under prefix tolerance and 6 as a bare token is a token census, not a petition-onset census - two of the six bare sites are third-person perfects (3:1, 3:36), so as petition onsets to the divine name the sites number 5 (1:9, 1:11, 1:20, 2:20 bare; 5:1 prefixed). The mark layer cannot corroborate either way at this seam: this poem carries one mark, the PE at 5:18, and no samekh (sweep: 1 mark over the poem's 22 verses), tier-3 weak and single-witness, and absence is never counterevidence.
rulings.remedy: (1) PROPOSAL ONLY - not a mechanical edit; requires explicit adoption before any span change: move the internal seam of the fifth poem from 5:11/5:12 to 5:10/5:11, so span becomes Lam.5.1-Lam.5.10 and the four-verse run stands whole at the head of the following unit. The seam then sits on the only person shift in that neighbourhood (last first-plural form at 5:10; 0 across 5:11-5:14), is weighed from both sides (first-plural catalogue in front, marked third-person run behind), stays inside the fifth poem parent so no poem seam is straddled, and puts no acrostic-letter boundary at stake because this poem carries no acrostic. (2) If the present seam is retained instead: device_notes must disclose the cross-seam run (verse-initial bare plural human-group noun plus third-plural verb at 5:11-5:14, no first-plural form in any of the four) as continuity argued against the unit; boundary_rationale must argue the close at 5:11 from both sides with a byte-named signal; confidence and frontier_flag_considered must be re-weighed to match a seam held on disclosed continuity. (3) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-state the ground for setting aside a cut after 5:6 with a criterion the chosen close itself satisfies. (4) boundary_rationale: replace the remember-digit with its object named (2 verses as a petition imperative; the root's third book-wide site is a negated third-person perfect) and the look-digit with both objects named (2 verses as a bare token; 4 verses under the single-letter prefix test - 1:11, 2:20, 3:63, 5:1). (5) boundary_rationale: call the onset a three-imperative chain and name the third imperative with its prefix, keeping the verse's ketiv/qere disclosure. TESTS the cure must pass - the tests that killed the original: every digit names its swept object and unit and reproduces at that object when the census members' form-class is read; no byte-true device spanning 5:11-5:14 straddles the unit's own seam undisclosed; every imperative in a cited verse is counted before that verse's onset is called doubled.

rulings.challenge_claim: Convergent on one row. One challenge holds that a structured signal key embeds the barred mark-layer term instead of confining that disclosure to prose. The other holds that the front seam opens inside a byte-marked block whose continuity the unit concedes in its first sentence without weighing it, that the mark at 5:18 is made to argue a seam rather than to corroborate one, that two signal keys have no byte object, and that the confession is placed at the span's centre when it is the fifth of seven verses.
rulings.grounds: Distinct defects, all sustained; the two challenges overlap only on the mark-layer key, where they are the same defect. FRONT SEAM (upheld, tier-1). The four-verse run adjudicated at the preceding close straddles this unit's front seam: 5:11-5:14 each open with a bare plural human-group noun - נָשִׁים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.11, byte tier), שָׂרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.12, byte tier), בַּחוּרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.13, byte tier), זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.14, byte tier) - followed by a third-plural verb, with no first-plural form in any of the four (sweep: 0 first-plural tokens over those 4 verses). The run's head stands one verse in front of the seam, and the unit's opening sentence concedes that the catalogue continues across it while weighing the seam from neither side. MARK LAYER (upheld, with its direction granted). This poem carries one mark, the PE at 5:18, and no samekh (sweep: 1 mark over the poem's 22 verses; 5 PE and 84 samekh over 89 marked verses book-wide), tier-3 weak and single-witness. A section mark after 5:18 does place 5:18 with what precedes, so the inference direction is right; the defect is the wording that makes the mark itself argue for keeping the verse inside the unit, which is the driver role the marker weighting forecloses - corroboration of a close already carried by a text signal is the most it can do. NEW FINDING in the same sentence: the exclusivity word attached to that mark ships with no adjacent digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit, though it is byte-true. SIGNAL KEYS (upheld). The mark-layer key fails twice: the disclosure belongs in prose only, and its hymnic namespace has no byte object inside this span, since the hymnic turn stands at 5:19 with the second-person address to the divine name, one verse past the close. The personification key has no byte object either: at 5:18 the mountain is resumed by the third-masculine-singular בֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.5.18, byte tier) as a place, and no daughter-formula of any class stands in this poem (sweep: 0 verses in the poem across the six formulas, whose book-wide totals are 8, 5, 3, 2, 2 and 2 verses). POSITION (upheld, low-grade). The span runs 7 verses and 5:16 is its fifth, so both the prose placement at the centre and the centre-named signal key are false to the span's own arithmetic. TWO FURTHER NEW FINDINGS neither challenge raises: the prose merges the two subjects of 5:13 - the young men bore the mill, the boys stumbled at the wood - into one clause about the young men; and the negative inventory window given as 5:12-5:17 stops one verse short of the span, though both inventories are in fact empty across the whole span (sweep: 0 ketiv/qere notes and 0 paseq segs over 5:12-5:18).
rulings.remedy: (1) observed_substrate_signals: delete the mark-layer key; the compliant prose disclosure already stands in device_notes. (2) observed_substrate_signals: delete or re-object the personification key - at its named verse the mountain is a place resumed by a third-masculine-singular pronoun; a desolation or closure key naming the desolate-mountain clause has a byte object, the personification key does not. (3) observed_substrate_signals and boundary_rationale: replace the centre-named key and the phrase placing the confession at the span's centre with the span's own arithmetic (fifth of seven verses). (4) strongest_rejected_alternative: strike the clause making the mark argue for the inclusion of 5:18, leaving it as corroboration of a close carried by the text signal; if the exclusivity word is kept, attach its digit-bearing sweep (1 mark in this poem, PE at 5:18, 0 samekh, single-witness, tier-3 weak, never conflated with samekh). (5) boundary_rationale: restore the second subject at 5:13. (6) device_notes: extend the negative ketiv/qere and paseq window to the whole span. (7) Front seam: the same choice as at the 5:11 close - adopt the proposed respan so the four-verse run opens this unit at 5:11, or disclose the straddling run in device_notes and argue the seam from both sides. TESTS the cure must pass: no signal key survives without a byte object at the verse it names; no mark-layer key stands in the signal list; every positional word is checked against the span's own verse count; every universal carries an adjacent digit naming its swept object and unit; every negative-inventory window covers the whole span. Corpus note for consolidation: signal keys naming the mark layer stand in 5 of the corpus's 26 rows, so this cure is a candidate corpus-wide order rather than a single-row edit.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span is byte-clean on every seam, quotation, census and disclosure test except its closing note, which calls 5:21 the unit's centre and says the two divine-name sites frame the petition between them: the span runs four verses so 5:21 is its third, the verse between the two sites is a why-question, and the span's only petition imperative stands at 5:21 itself.
rulings.grounds: Upheld in substance, refined on the challenge's own exclusivity digit. ARITHMETIC (upheld, tier-1 address signal with a false positional gloss): the span runs 4 verses and 5:21 is its third, so the centre placement is false to the span's own count; the divine name stands at 5:19 and 5:21 and at neither 5:20 nor 5:22 (sweep: 3 verses in this poem - 5:1, 5:19, 5:21), and what stands between the two sites is the why-question of 5:20, whose verbs are second-masculine-singular imperfects carrying first-plural object suffixes - not a petition. So the framed material is not the petition, and the petition stands at one of the frames. REFINEMENT: the challenge calls the return-imperative the span's only petition imperative; the bytes carry a second one in the same verse, חַדֵּ֥שׁ (oshb:Lam.5.21, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, the variant standing at the return-verb, which the unit splices and discloses). Both imperatives sit at 5:21, so the finding survives intact and only its exclusivity digit is wrong - an object-of-the-digit correction, not a rescue of the unit. The rest of what the challenge confirms reproduces here: the address return at 5:19 opens the span after verses carrying no divine name; the one paseq site across the fourth and fifth poems stands at 5:21 (sweep: 1 seg, count-only, single-witness); the ketiv/qere note at 5:21 is disclosed in the field carrying the splice; and this poem carries no acrostic, none being claimed.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the centre wording with the span's own arithmetic (5:21 is the third of the span's four verses) and re-state the frame - the two address sites stand at 5:19 and 5:21 with the why-question of 5:20 between them, and the span's petition imperatives (return and renew) both stand at 5:21, at one of the frames rather than between them. TEST the cure must pass - the test that killed the original: every positional word reproduces against the span's own verse count, and any material described as framed is the material actually standing between the two cited sites.
